attributes.action: Review the Supreme Court's sex ruling against Parliament's Equality Act record
attributes.additional_details: The Supreme Court's 2025 judgment interpreted "sex", "man" and "woman" in the Equality Act 2010 as biological sex and considered section 9 of the Gender Recognition Act 2004. Parliament should examine whether this interpretation reflects the legislation and the parliamentary record when these Acts were passed. We ask the Government to compare the judgment with Hansard, ministerial statements and explanatory material, particularly concerning section 9's "for all purposes" provision.
attributes.background: Require the Government to review the Supreme Court's interpretation in For Women Scotland Ltd v The Scottish Ministers [2025] UKSC 16 against the parliamentary record for the Gender Recognition Act 2004 and Equality Act 2010, and report its findings to Parliament.

rejection.details:
The UK Government does not review rulings of the Supreme Court.

The Supreme Court is the final court of appeal. The courts are independent of Government, Parliament and other external influence; this is called judicial independence and impartiality.

You can find out about the role of the Supreme Court here: https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cbp-9536/

You may also be interested in this House of Commons Library briefing on the Supreme Court judgment on the meaning of “sex” in the Equality Act 2010: https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cbp-10259/

You may wish to support one of these petitions:

Disapprove the draft Equality Act 2010 guidance laid on 21 May 2026 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/770527

Amend Equality Act so “sex” refers to gender identity, not biological sex 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/780014

Review Equality Act 2010 to protect Transgender, Non-binary & Intersex people 
https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/756041
